topic: How do distributed satellite constellations impact orbital configuration trade-offs between coverage and inter-satellite interference mitigation?
consensus_response: Distributed satellite constellations significantly impact orbital configuration trade-offs between coverage and inter-satellite interference mitigation. The array factor's impact on signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is primarily due to satellites' positioning, causing interference effects. As satellites are spaced closer together, the main lobe of the array factor broadens, reducing SNR and increasing interference. Each satellite added increases the number of potential interferers by a factor of N (number of satellites), decreasing SNR by approximately 10 log(N) dB. This implies a decrease in system capacity and an increase in interference mitigation costs. Orbital diversity can help mitigate inter-satellite interference, but introduces new challenges such as increased complexity and cost.
